I found several relevant papers on process reward models from May 2026 and related recent work. Here are the key results:

## Most Recent (May 2026)

A new arXiv paper proposes a method for training unsupervised PRMs (uPRM) that requires no human supervision, neither at the level of step-by-step annotations nor through ground-truth verification of final answers. The key idea is to define a scoring function, derived from LLM next-token probabilities, that jointly assesses candidate positions of first erroneous steps across a batch of reasoning trajectories.

The results show that uPRM achieves up to 15% absolute accuracy improvements over the LLM-as-a-Judge in identifying first erroneous steps on the ProcessBench dataset, performs comparably to supervised PRMs as a verifier, and enables more robust policy optimization when used as a reward signal in reinforcement learning.

Great! I found the research paper you were looking for. Here are the key details:

## SCOPE: Compress Mathematical Reasoning Steps for Efficient Automated Process Annotation

SCOPE is a novel compression-based approach that significantly reduces annotation costs, published in May 2025 on arXiv (paper 2505.14419).

### Key Approach

The method translates natural language reasoning steps into code and normalizes them through Abstract Syntax Tree, then merges equivalent steps to construct a prefix tree. 

### Efficiency Gains

Unlike simulation-based methods that waste numerous samples on estimation, SCOPE leverages a compression-based prefix tree where each root-to-leaf path serves as a training sample, reducing the complexity from O(NMK) to O(N). The researchers constructed a large-scale dataset containing 196K samples with only 5% of the computational resources required by previous methods.

### Authors and Affiliation

The paper was authored by Huimin Xu, Xin Mao, Feng-Lin Li, Xiaobao Wu, Wang Chen, Wei Zhang, and Anh Tuan Luu from Nanyang Technological University, Shopee, and SEA Group.

You can access the full paper on arXiv at: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.14419
